tasks.title: Trace the BRS to the April statement
tasks.prompt: Pallavi’s 31 March BRS lists seven items. Trace each cheque and deposit to the April statement: same number, same amount, the day it cleared. Check the bank’s own entries against the March statement and the advice behind each. For an exception, pick what is wrong and the entry it needs. Your calls go to Aditi when you move on.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your BRS calls to Aditi?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Aditi. You can read your calls but not change them.

hints: Put each cheque and deposit beside the April statement: same number, same amount. For a cheque that never turns up, read the date written on it.
An entry the bank made in March that the books don’t have is booked at 31 March, whenever its advice reached accounts.

options.label: Not in the books
options.short: bank entry not in the books

options.label: Reverse it: debit cash credit, credit the payee
Debit bank charges, credit cash credit
Debit cash credit, credit the customer
No entry: it will clear in the next statement

fields.label: Your note for the file
fields.placeholder: For example: paid 9 April, same number and amount (or what is wrong)

items.label: Cheque 418806 · Moshi Corrugators
items.note: Fine. Cheque 418806 for ₹2,92,793 was paid on 5 April: same number, same amount, ten days after it was written. That is how a cheque on a BRS should behave.

items.label: Cheque 418811 · Talegaon Electricals
items.note: Fine. Paid on 8 April, with the number and amount the BRS lists.

items.label: Cheque 418814 · Nighojkar Security
items.note: Fine. Nighojkar banked it quickly: paid on 2 April for ₹30,160.

items.label: Cheque 417652 · Shirur Metrology Labs
items.note: Exception. Written on 26 November and never presented. After three months the bank won’t pay it, and Shirur has lost it anyway. Reverse it: the cash credit comes down by ₹44,660 and Shirur is owed again.

items.label: Deposit · Bilal Ferrous Traders
items.note: Fine. The bank stamped the slip on 31 March and credited the cheque on 2 April. Paid in during March, cleared in April: an honest reconciling item.

items.label: Bank debit · Locker rent
items.note: Exception, a small one. The bank took ₹2,360 on 31 March and the books don’t have it. Pallavi’s note says book it in April; it belongs to March. Debit bank charges, credit the cash credit.

items.label: Bank credit · NEFT from Lothal Motors
items.note: Exception. Lothal’s ₹12,64,000 reached the bank on 30 March; the books took it on 6 April, when Harshad passed on the advice. At 31 March the cash credit and Lothal’s balance are both overstated. Book the receipt in March.

tasks.title: Write to Mahesh about the confirmations
tasks.prompt: You showed Aditi Varun’s chat. She wants one mail from you to Mahesh about the bank’s certificate and Kshitij’s reply, saying what we do with each. Pick the right line for each part; the chat and both papers are in Documents. The mail goes to Aditi when you move on.

lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change it after this.
lockOnLeave.done: With Aditi. You can read your mail but not change it.

hints: Ask of each paper: did it reach us straight from the bank or from Kshitij? Whatever passed through Tamhini, however genuine it looks, we ask for again ourselves.

freeText.label: Your own line for the mail

options.text: Thank you for the bank’s certificate. We can’t use it as the bank’s confirmation to us: it is addressed to Tamhini and came through you, so it is not the bank’s reply to the auditors.
options.why: The bank wrote to Tamhini, at Tamhini’s request, and the paper reached us through Mahesh. It isn’t a reply to us, and it says nothing about the deposits, the loans or the guarantee.

options.text: Thank you for the bank’s certificate. We can use it as the bank’s confirmation: it is on the bank’s letterhead, signed and sealed by the branch manager, and its balance matches the statement to the rupee.
options.why: Letterhead, seal and a matching balance don’t make it ours. Its last line says it was “issued at the specific request of the customer”: it answers Tamhini, not us. It covers only the cash credit.

options.text: Thank you for the bank’s certificate. We can’t use it until the branch manager confirms the balance to us on the phone, so we will call the branch today and note his answer on the file.
options.why: A phone call is not a written reply to us, so it can’t stand as the bank’s confirmation. The bank has to write to us directly.

options.text: Please sign our request to the branch manager on Tamhini’s letterhead. It asks the bank to confirm to us, at our office, the cash credit balance of ₹8,82,61,002 at 31 March, which we have filled in from the bank statement for them.
options.why: Only the cash credit, and already filled in. The bank would agree a number we gave it, and nobody would ask about anything else Tamhini has with the bank.

options.text: Please sign our request to the branch manager on Tamhini’s letterhead. It asks the bank to write to us with every account, deposit, loan, guarantee and lien at 31 March, and the interest accrued, leaving every amount blank.
options.why: Tamhini signs it, so the bank will answer; it asks for the reply at our office, so the answer comes to us. Asking for everything, with the amounts blank, makes the bank read its own books. That is how liens and guarantees come out.

options.text: Please sign our request to the branch manager on Tamhini’s letterhead. It asks the bank to send Tamhini a fresh certificate covering every account, deposit, loan and guarantee, which you can then pass on to us when it comes.
options.why: Every account this time, but back to Tamhini again. A reply that passes through the client is the problem we started with.

options.text: Kshitij’s reply is fine to keep. Harshad knows their people well, and their sales office has confirmed our exact balance of ₹3,58,60,691 to him in writing, on the same day that he asked for it.
options.why: Knowing the people is the problem, not the proof. Kshitij’s sales office writing to Tamhini’s sales head is not Kshitij’s accounts confirming to us.

options.text: Kshitij’s reply is fine to keep if Harshad signs a printout of the whole mail chain as a true copy, so that someone at Tamhini takes responsibility for the figure we file.
options.why: Tamhini signing for its own debtor proves nothing about Kshitij’s books. The confirmation has to come from Kshitij, to us.

options.text: Kshitij’s reply has the same problem. It went from their sales office to Harshad, then to you and to Varun, so it never came to us, and we can’t tell who at Kshitij checked it.
options.why: Kshitij’s mail says “as discussed on the phone”: their sales office agreed a figure on a call with Harshad. Their accounts team has to check it in their books and write to us.

options.text: Please sign the fresh request to Kshitij too. It goes to their head of accounts at the Bhosari address on their purchase orders, stating ₹3,58,60,691 as per your books, with replies only to our office.
options.why: The right person, at an address we checked ourselves, a request that states the balance, and a reply that can only come to us.

options.text: Please sign the fresh request to Kshitij too. Harshad can hand it to their sales office on his next visit; it states ₹3,58,60,691 as per your books and asks their accounts team to reply to him by mail.
options.why: Same route, same problem. Tamhini’s sales team must have no hand in carrying the request or the reply.

options.text: Please sign the fresh request to Kshitij too. It goes to their head of accounts, states ₹3,58,60,691 as per your books, and says that if we hear nothing in seven days, we will take it as agreed.
options.why: Silence is not agreement. A request that wants a reply only if they disagree is the weakest kind of confirmation, and not for a balance of ₹3.59 crore.

options.text: Your office can courier both requests today, and Harshad can follow up with Kshitij and collect their reply, since he speaks to their team every week.
options.why: Once Tamhini sends and chases, we no longer control what goes out or what comes back.

options.text: We will email both requests from Tamhini’s accounts mailbox today, so that Kshitij and the bank see they come from you and can simply reply to that mailbox.
options.why: Sent from Tamhini’s mailbox, the requests bring every reply back to Tamhini. Mahesh’s signature on the letter is authority enough; the sending is ours.

options.text: We will post both requests ourselves today and send a reminder if nothing reaches us in ten days. Please ask Harshad not to take it up with Kshitij.
options.why: We post the requests and the reminders, and the replies come only to us. That control is what makes a confirmation worth having.

tasks.title: Recompute FD interest and tie it out
tasks.prompt: Monday 10 May. The bank’s reply came on Friday, and Form 168 now shows its January–March rows. Recompute each deposit’s interest for 2026–27 from its terms, then tie the books to it and to Form 168: enter what the books must add, 0 where nothing. The papers are in Documents.
hints: FD-1’s last payment was 18 March, FD-2’s last addition 12 March. Work FD-2’s days on the bank’s balance after that addition, not the ledger’s: the ledger is net of tax.
Form 168 shows what the bank paid or credited in the year, not the year’s interest income.
tasks.note: Count days from the day after the last payment or addition, to 31 March, as each deposit’s terms say. Round each figure to the rupee.

notes.r6.fd1: Nothing. Form 168 is ₹748 short of the books: this bank deducts tax on FD-1 only when it pays, so last March’s 13 days sit in June’s row and this March’s are missing. By law it should have deducted at 31 March, as on FD-2.

notes.r9.fd1: Nothing. Form 168 and the books agree.

hints: For each difference, find the date each side booked it: money on its way at 31 March, or an entry one side hasn’t made.
A cover returned undelivered is no reply at all. A request the client stopped was never sent.

principles: A BRS item clears in the next statement with the same number and amount, or it needs an entry or an answer.
A confirmation counts only when it reaches us straight from the party; one that passed through the client is a lead, never a confirmation.
No reply means alternative work, never a tick. A difference means finding why: money on its way needs no entry; a wrong or missing entry is put right.

interview.q: The client’s accountant hands you the bank’s balance certificate. Will you accept it?

outline: No. It’s addressed to the client and came through them: not the bank’s reply to us.

outline: Check the address myself and send a reminder; a letter returned undelivered also counts as no reply.
